core_obligations: Definition of the map: describe the image of a tableau by inserting the entry one at the front of the first row and its conjugate at the end, and record the resulting tableau (proof lines 965-972).

Well-definedness: verify that the result is again a Kashiwara-Nakashima tableau of the shifted shape, using the relations on the entries and treating separately the cases in which the entries at the junction are the extremal ones (proof lines 973-1015).

Crystal compatibility: check that the map commutes with the crystal operators, distinguishing the operators acting on the first row from those acting on the second and using the comparison tool (proof lines 1015-1030).
Conclusion: the compatibility with the operators, together with the injectivity of the construction, exhibits the map as an embedding of crystals (proof lines 1030-1039).
proof_roadmap: The insertions defining the map (proof lines 965-972).
Well-definedness through the relations and the case analysis (proof lines 973-1015).
Compatibility with the crystal operators and conclusion (proof lines 1015-1039).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The proposition constructs an embedding of the crystal of the highest weight entry into the crystal of the weight shifted by twice the first fundamental weight (statement lines 959-962). The proof (proof lines 964-1039) defines the map by explicit insertions on Kashiwara-Nakashima tableaux, verifies through a case analysis governed by the relations on entries that the image is again such a tableau, and checks compatibility with the crystal operators using the author's comparison lemma. H3: a long combinatorial argument resting on three inputs.

Remaining cases: otherwise the function vanishes, which covers the remaining dispositions of the parameters and completes the formula (proof lines 2908-2917).

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the comparison of translated weights that the proof performs case by case.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's description of the translations attached to the roots of the form used in the proof

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary order relations among the entries of the weight
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypotheses of the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Provide the inequalities between the coordinates that are compared in the two parts of the lemma.

core_obligations: First part, reduction: the index corresponding to a root of the stated form is a multiple of four, and the assumption on the parameter makes the translation a reflection, so that the comparison becomes a comparison of multiples (proof lines 2047-2052).

First part, comparison: applying the Bruhat order criterion to the two multiples yields the asserted inequality, and the case in which the parameter is not a multiple of four is reduced to the previous one by a direct comparison of the remaining coordinates (proof lines 2052-2070).

Second part: assuming instead the inequality on the first coordinate, the same case analysis with the criterion gives that every translated weight lies below the fixed weight, which is the second assertion (proof lines 2070-2089).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to a reflection and comparison of multiples (proof lines 2047-2052).
The first assertion in both cases (proof lines 2052-2070).
The second assertion by the same analysis (proof lines 2070-2089).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves two monotonicity statements for translated highest weights: under an inequality on the first coordinate of the translated parameter, the translations attached to the roots of the stated form decrease along the multiples, and under an inequality on the first coordinate of the original weight they stay below the fixed weight (statement lines 2041-2045). The proof (proof lines 2046-2089) reduces to reflections, applies the Bruhat order criterion, and handles the remaining cases by explicit comparison of coordinates. H2: a short case analysis resting on three inputs.
